title: This iPhone App Turns Your Lost Scrolling Hours Black
summary:
Your phone can quietly eat hours. Oh My Hours, a new app for iPhone, tries to make that lost time easy to see. Instead of long lists and menus, it turns each day into a row of circles, one for every hour. If you spend time in an app you marked as a distraction, that hour's circle turns black.

You choose the distractions yourself. You can pick whole groups, such as social media apps and games, or choose apps one by one. By default, even a few seconds in a distracting app can mark the whole hour as lost. The idea is that a looser rule could tempt you to use a little free time after every hour resets.

You can start using Oh My Hours for free on iOS. There is no sign of an Android version yet. Paying $10 a year or $20 for lifetime access lets you choose what counts as a lost hour or day, change the time threshold, and see month and year views that show patterns over weeks and months. You can also set quiet hours, when any distracting app use marks every hour in that quiet zone, not just one. If an hour is marked by mistake, such as a finger slipping and opening Instagram, you can reset it. The app can also export your stats as a CSV file.

Other apps take different approaches. One Sec pauses for a breathing exercise before you continue or back out. Forest grows a virtual forest while you leave your phone alone. ScreenZen adds pauses and challenges, Roots schedules phone-free periods, and Brick uses a small tap device to block apps. The black circle is the point: one glance shows whether the day went to scrolling, or to something better.
why_it_matters: When lost time is visible at a glance, it is harder to ignore how much of a day goes to scrolling, and easier to decide whether that time matches what a person actually wants to do with it.
